lines.text: 5. **"Rise" in the ordinary sense (R8) is not empty.** 55 of 95 verses carry an M-code: knowing, release, sin and confession (M15, M59, M56, M60). Examples are "Rise and be baptized and wash away your sins" (Act 22:16) and "authority … to forgive sins … Rise" (Mat 9:6). The verb is the act; what moves is elsewhere in the verse (rule 73).

- **No current claim states anything about the raised body itself.** That covers the seed and the body, the four contrasts, Christ the firstfruits, the change "in a moment", the tent and the clothing, the body made like his, no marrying, and the two resurrections. Claim 10-4 names Rom 8:23 and 1Co 15:42–44, but as held, "not in the reading".

findings.text: 1.3 What the counts point to (for the reading to test): The body with the inner being (B4) is the densest group: 46 of 49 verses carry an M-code, M47 in 16. The body words sit beside heart, soul, spirit and mind, and beside sin (M56, M58) and purity (M61). This is the present body, not the raised one.; The changed body (A1, A6) also leans to M47 (8 and 3 verses). The changed-body verses set the body beside the inner seat too.; The resurrection itself carries little inner-being vocabulary. In R1 (the debate) only 5 of 13 verses carry an M-code. R2's ten verses carry one each of eight different codes. Where the R groups do carry codes, they are: judgment, in the coming resurrection (R5: M26 in 7); faith, trust and remembering, beside Christ raised (R4: M13, M19, M81); faintness, in R4 and R5 (M24); Glory divides.; G2, glory among people, carries authority, seeking, desire, wickedness, pride and deceit (M72, M83, M18, M58, M08, M14). This is glory as something sought, an inner act.; G1, glory to come, carries faintness, judgment and prayer (M24, M26, M42). The verses set it beside suffering and losing heart.; G3, glory given to God, carries praise (M22), with fear (M01) and turning (M11) in Revelation's "fear God and give him glory" and "they did not repent and give him glory".; "Rise" in the ordinary sense (R8) is not empty. 55 of 95 verses carry an M-code: knowing, release, sin and confession (M15, M59, M56, M60). Examples are "Rise and be baptized and wash away your sins" (Act 22:16) and "authority … to forgive sins … Rise" (Mat 9:6). The verb is the act; what moves is elsewhere in the verse (rule 73).
